The delayed onset after trauma raises suspicion for post-traumatic syringomyelia, though Chiari I remains the most common cause and is appropriately being evaluated with cine CSF flow imaging. EMG/NCS is warranted to rule out mimics (e.g., multifocal motor neuropathy, ALS), but the symmetry, sensory symptoms, and imaging confirmation make primary spinal cord pathology definitive. Metabolic, autoimmune, and infectious workup is appropriate for exclusion but none are supported by current data.

[EVIDENCE]  
- 1-year history of burning cervical and upper extremity pain → classic presentation of spinothalamic tract involvement in syringomyelia  
- Bilateral hand paresthesias → consistent with dorsal horn or central cord sensory disruption  
- Progressive bilateral hand weakness over 3 months → reflects symmetric anterior horn cell damage at cervical enlargement (C8–T1)  
- Impaired grip strength and increased object-dropping → functional correlate of intrinsic hand muscle weakness (lower motor neuron pattern)  
- No gait instability → suggests sparing of corticospinal tracts in lateral columns (i.e., no significant long-tract involvement beyond central cord)  
- No visible muscle atrophy → consistent with subacute (3-month) progression; atrophy may not yet be apparent  
- Cervical and upper thoracic spinal MRI demonstrates a syrinx spanning those levels → direct structural evidence of syringomyelia  
- Prior motor vehicle accident 3 years ago with delayed symptom onset → compatible with post-traumatic syringomyelia (though Chiari I is more common)  
- Provisional impression identifies syringomyelia and central cord involvement → corroborates pattern-matching by expert clinician  

[GAPS]  
- Absence of documented sensory examination findings for light touch, vibration, proprioception, or pinprick mapping → prevents confirmation of dissociated sensory loss (key diagnostic feature)  
- No EMG/NCS results reported → cannot yet confirm or exclude anterior horn cell denervation vs. peripheral nerve/motor neuron disease  
- No brain MRI results yet available → Chiari I malformation status unknown; critical for determining etiology and surgical planning  
- No cine CSF flow imaging results → inability to assess for CSF obstruction at foramen magnum or spinal level  
- No assessment of bowel/bladder function or Horner syndrome → subtle autonomic or descending sympathetic tract involvement not evaluated  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Syringomyelia
